messages:
maria: heads-up — while triaging partner webhook errors in staging I found a base64 blob in logs that decodes to a GCP service-account key. not in prod. tagging sec-oncall and infra.
kevin: :rotating_light: thanks. can you paste the log line (redacted) and the blob id? we need to confirm it's a private key and who it belongs to.
maria: pasted below (redacted): `POST /webhook 200 ... payload=***REDACTED***` blob starts with: `ewogICJ0eXBlIjogInNlcnZpY2VfYWNjb3VudCIsCiAgImNsaWVudF9lbWFpbCI6ICJwYXJ0bmVyQG1haWwuY29tIiwKICAi...`
sasha: infra-bot flagged this earlier as sensitive. infra-bot, share detection details?
infra-bot: [Alert] sensitive-blob-detected channel=partner-webhook env=staging severity=high pattern=base64_gcp_sa_key ticket=SEC-3124
nora: first things first: revoke that key and rotate. then rewrap any wrapped blobs. who can run revocation now?
kevin: on it. steps I'm doing: 1) identify SA email by decoding partial blob 2) list keys 3) revoke compromised key 4) create new key and re-deploy to partner if needed 5) scan logs for other occurrences.
maria: decoded metadata shows `serviceAccount: partner-ingest@redwood-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (truncated). no other envs seen so far.
kevin: running: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=partner-ingest@redwood-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-staging --format=json` -> found key ID `a1b2c3d4` created 2026-03-15T02:11:00Z
kevin: revoking now: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete a1b2c3d4 --iam-account=partner-ingest@redwood-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-staging` (done) :white_check_mark:
kevin: creating replacement key and uploading to Vault: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys create - --iam-account=partner-ingest@redwood-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-staging | vault write secret/data/partner/ingest/key @-`
sasha: hold — before we push a raw key into secret/text, we should use Vault's transit wrap or GCP KMS envelope encryption. prefer: put key material into Vault with transit encryption or use GCP KMS to rewrap and then store only ciphertext in vault.
nora: agree. plan: - put new key into GCS encrypted with KMS key projects/redwood-kms/locations/global/keyRings/rotations/cryptoKeys/partner-wrap - store wrapped ciphertext in Vault (secret/partner/ingest/wrapped_key) - rotate service account in partner integration list.
maria: scanning logs for other leaks now: `grep -R "partner-ingest" /var/logs/webhooks/* | grep -i base64` — found 3 lines from last 2 days in staging only.
kevin: quick QA checklist for this incident: 1) revoke compromised key (done) 2) create new key & wrap with KMS (in progress) 3) update partner integration with new public credential flow (needs owner) 4) run cluster-wide scan for base64-encoded blobs and block uploads containing SA JSON 5) update CI/CD to not accept raw keys
maria: I'm creating SEC ticket with remediation checklist and cross-ref to runbook: https://go/infra-sec/runbooks/sa-key-leak (internal link)
sasha: can we enable Vault audit logging for secrets write/read around partner path so we capture who accessed the wrapped blob? nora, can your team add a retention of 90d for that path?
nora: yes, I'll schedule audit sink: `vault audit enable file file_path=/var/log/vault/partner_ingest_audit.log` and then push to centralized logging. will set 90d retention in LUCI.
kevin: additional step: check KMS key policy to ensure only CI and Ops have decrypt permissions. run: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy partner-wrap --keyring=rotations --location=global --project=redwood-kms` and remove any broad principals.
sasha: also add automated alert: if any plaintext-looking SA JSON appears in logs, drop to quarantine and open incident. infra: can we add a log processor rule in staging?
infra-bot: [Task] created log-processor-rule staging: quarantine_on_sa_json_match assigned=infra-team ticket=OPS-789
maria: partner informed via secure channel, they confirmed they will update their integration after we provide new wrapped key. asked for a signed ack and date.
kevin: runbook note: for Vault->GCP KMS integration we prefer storing ciphertext in Vault instead of plaintext. Example rewrap flow:
```
# generate key
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create key.json --iam-account=partner-ingest@... --project=redwood-staging
# envelope encrypt with KMS
gcloud kms encrypt --location=global --keyring=rotations --key=partner-wrap --plaintext-file=key.json --ciphertext-file=key.json.enc
# store ciphertext in Vault
vault kv put secret/partner/ingest wrapped_ciphertext=@key.json.enc
```
kevin: also adding a quick detection regex to log-processor: `(\{\s*"type"\s*:\s*"service_account"|"private_key"\s*:)` to catch SA JSON blocks.
maria: who owns notifying compliance for the exposure (P0)?
kevin: sasha will notify compliance and CS where necessary. sasha?
sasha: on it — will send summary and exec notification within the hour. tagging oncall for SOC monitoring.
oncall: monitoring turned on for staging ingress spikes and outbound egress to unknown IPs. will escalate if anything odd.
nora: post-incident tasks: 1) add lint to partner integration to reject raw keys 2) add pre-commit hook to infra repos to forbid `key.json` artifacts 3) rotate KMS wrapping keys if we detect reuse across partners
maria: timeline: detection 1768504322, revocation 1768505600, new wrapped key stored 1768508000, partner ack expected by 1768512000. closing notes will go to SEC-3124.
kevin: closing checklist item: also run `gcloud logging read "resource.type=project AND textPayload:partner-ingest" --project=redwood-staging --limit=1000` to capture other exposures.
sasha: thanks everyone. good catch. we should include sample playbook in runbook and run a tabletop next week. :thumbsup:
